finding: Dead-owner and corrupt-marker resets unlink whatever marker is current, so two concurrent calls can each start a worktree for one session
why: Both calls read the same old marker, A unlinks it and records and spawns a new move, then B's unconditional unlink deletes A's fresh marker and B records and spawns a second one, leaving two worktrees and two /cd lines.
fix: Claim the stale marker atomically (os.replace it to a unique aside name and treat FileNotFoundError as lost-the-claim, then re-plan) instead of unlink(missing_ok=True).
evidence: `marker.unlink(missing_ok=True)  # an earlier session's worktree, not this one's` / `return plan(place, envelope, facts)` (same pattern at line 148 for the corrupt branch). Failing input: two parallel tool calls in one resumed session whose recorded worktree owner is dead.

finding: The RETRY_AFTER restart is not claimed: concurrent callers (or a retry while the first helper still runs) each touch and spawn a helper for the same name
why: Two parallel guard calls at age >= 180s both pass the age check and spawn; the loser fails create-worktree with 'already taken' and writes `error` into the marker, which can land after the winner's `created` and survive.
fix: Make the restart exclusive (e.g. O_EXCL sidecar per retry, or compare-and-bump the marker mtime) so only one caller spawns.
evidence: `if Path(chosen["path"]).exists() or age < RETRY_AFTER: return chosen` / `marker.touch()` followed by unconditional `spawn([...])`; scripts/create-worktree:418 `[[ ! -e "$DEST" ]] || error_exit "worktree ... already taken ..."` is the loser's error, written by scripts/afk-move.py:272 `record(args.marker, **{"error": error})`.

finding: When all REPLACE_TRIES swaps fail the outcome is dropped silently and never logged
why: A lost `error` outcome leaves the marker without it, so every refusal for the next 180s says the worktree 'is being created' for a creation that already failed, and the move log (documented to hold every exception) has no trace.
fix: Log the exhausted swap (and the swallowed OSError/ValueError) via log(), and consider a longer or backing-off retry since antivirus scans on Windows can hold the new file longer than 0.5s.
evidence: `for _ in range(REPLACE_TRIES): try: os.replace(whole, target) ... except PermissionError: time.sleep(0.1)` then `except (OSError, ValueError): pass` and `whole.unlink(missing_ok=True)` with no log(); module docstring: 'Every step, wait result and exception goes to ... .log'.

finding: Possible swallowed failure: `record` drops the creation outcome without a log line when the swap or the read fails, or after the PermissionError retries run out
why: This helper writes the only `created`/`error` outcome the marker carries, and its own `log()` is the sole diagnostic channel, yet a lost outcome leaves no trace in `<name>.log`, so a failed creation can stay reported as 'being created'.
fix: Log (via `log`) the exception or exhausted-retry case before returning, and keep the best-effort cleanup.
evidence: afk-move.py:137-138 `except (OSError, ValueError):\n        pass`; the for-loop at :131-136 falls out silently after `REPLACE_TRIES` PermissionErrors; `log()` is defined at :70 and is used by every other step

finding: Blocked-swap test stubs time.sleep to a no-op and never asserts the back-off, so the retry window it names is unproven
why: afk-move.py:136 retries 5 times with time.sleep(0.1) so that 'half a second outlasts' a reader's brief hold (afk-move.py:37); deleting that sleep leaves len(tries)==REPLACE_TRIES and the old-marker asserts green while the 5 retries burn in microseconds and no longer outlast a reader.
fix: Record the stubbed sleep calls and assert they are REPLACE_TRIES-1 or more calls of about 0.1 s (or assert the summed wait is at least 0.4 s).
evidence: monkeypatch.setattr(module.time, "sleep", lambda seconds: None) ... assert marker.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == before and len(tries) == module.REPLACE_TRIES

finding: The transient 'another call is still writing it - try the command again' error is wrapped by the guard as 'could not be created ... Fix that, or run create-worktree --name'

Fix that, or run `{root}/scripts/create-worktree --name <name>` and continue there.`

finding: plan returns the recorded move with its stale `error` key when the worktree exists or a retry has just been spawned
why: The guard treats any `error` as failure (protected_branch_guard.py:455) so it prints 'could not be created' and no /cd line even though a retry is running or the worktree is there; the fix lands only on a later call.
fix: Drop `error` from the returned dict when the path exists or after the retry spawn (the helper re-adds it on failure).
evidence: `return chosen` (line 157) and the retry fall-through to `return chosen` (line 165) with `chosen` read from a marker holding the helper's `error`; guard: `if chosen.get("error"): ... "the session worktree could not be created"`.

finding: A spawn failure after the marker is recorded leaves a marker with no helper behind it
why: Popen raising (e.g. unusable sys.executable) propagates after record() succeeded, so later calls within 180s return the recorded move as in progress and promise a path nothing is creating.
fix: On a spawn exception, remove the marker this call created (or record `error` into it) before re-raising.
evidence: `created = record(marker, chosen)` (line 135) ... `spawn([sys.executable, str(PLUGIN_ROOT / "scripts" / "afk-move.py"), ...], owner_env())` with no except; next call hits `or age < RETRY_AFTER: return chosen`.

finding: record() gives up after 5 PermissionErrors and drops the outcome silently, where the old code still wrote it
why: A reader holding the marker for more than 0.4 s now loses the `created` or `error` outcome with no trace. The marker keeps its pre-outcome body, so a creation failure is never recorded and the session is respawned after RETRY_AFTER under the same name (inferred from reading; not run).
fix: After the retries, write the body in place as the old fallback did (the h2_move reader tolerates a torn read), or log the lost outcome on the helper's log path.
evidence: afk-move.py:131-138 `for _ in range(REPLACE_TRIES): try: os.replace(whole, target); return / except PermissionError: time.sleep(0.1)` then `except (OSError, ValueError): pass`; the loop falls through to `whole.unlink(...)` with no write of `body`

finding: 'Still being written' test depends on wall-clock age under 10 s without pinning the mtime
why: The marker is written with the current mtime and the test relies on plan() running within WRITING (10 s) of that write; a stalled runner turns the expected 'another call is still writing it' error into an unlink-and-replan, whereas the sibling corrupt-marker test pins mtime with os.utime.
fix: Set the marker mtime explicitly with os.utime(marker, (now, now)) or patch module.age_of to return 0 so the verdict does not depend on scheduler speed.
evidence: marker.write_text("{\"name\": ", encoding="utf-8") ... chosen = module.plan(...) ; hooks/lib/h2_move.py:145 `if age is not None and age < WRITING:`
